en.html:
By the time we set foot on Enoshima, the night was already well advanced. Finding a small boat had taken time; handling it, we had little practice at. Dawn could not be more than a few hours away.

Tonight, it seemed, we would have to content ourselves with a preliminary look. Never mind making a circuit of the island: even observing the shogunate laboratory looked unlikely.

Everyone spoke little, naturally, because we were keeping out of sight. Even so, on a picnic I doubt the talk would have been lively.

Nobody said it, but surely all of us had already noticed. This feeling of nothingness was too cold on the skin to overlook.

There was no sign of life.

There were no animals.

Wild creatures with keen senses do not, in any case, show themselves before men. But not a footfall running far away, not a faint breath, not even a wary gaze at the intruders: none of it at all? Really?

This, on Enoshima, where the environment should have been carefully protected. What was going on?
